BiblicalUsage: Baasha was the king of Israel who conspired against Nadab, took the throne, and reigned twenty-four years in Tirzah, warring with Asa of Judah all their days and building Ramah to shut Judah in. The word of the Lord came against him because he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel to sin, and his house was cut off, as the house of Jeroboam had been.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Baasha's story is the pattern of every king who takes the throne by murder and keeps it by idolatry: God gives the kingdom, and God takes it away, and the house falls exactly as he said.
RelatedPeople: Baasha, King of Israel; King Asa
